description: Eight modelled strings sharing one bridge, so striking one sets its neighbours ringing; the display is the instrument and the strings are strummed with the mouse or driven from gates

params.text: Sets how much of the shared wooden body is heard behind the strings
Sets how strongly a ringing string sets its neighbours going through the shared bridge
Sets how long a string rings, 0.15 to 20 seconds
Sets how quickly the high partials die away, which darkens a string as it rings; the filter is held above ten times each string's own pitch so a high string is not silenced
Sets how hard the exciter is, which sets the brightness of a strike, a pluck or a bow
Sets how far apart in time the strings are struck by one strum, and which way the strum runs: anticlockwise for upward, clockwise for downward
Transposes the whole instrument, -12 to 12 semitones
Transposes the whole instrument, -4 to 3 octaves
Picks the auto-player's pattern, from eighteen
Sets how many of the auto-player's notes are actually played
Switches the auto-player on and off
Returns the auto-player's pattern to its start on each press
Picks the scale the string tunings are snapped to, or leaves them free at the first position

inputs.text: Changes the body resonance, ±5V added to the body knob
Changes the bridge coupling, ±5V added to the coupling knob
Changes the ring time, ±5V added to the decay knob
Changes how fast the high partials die, ±5V added to the damping knob
Changes the exciter hardness, ±5V added to the pick knob
Changes the strum spread and direction, ±5V added to the spread knob
Transposes the instrument, a volt per octave snapped to semitones, added to the root knob
Transposes the instrument, one volt per octave, added to the octave knob
Transposes the whole instrument as a volt per octave
A rise strums every string that is switched on
Sets each string's velocity, 0-10V, one polyphonic channel per string
Each rise advances the auto-player's pattern by one step
A rise returns the auto-player's pattern to its start
Picks the auto-player's pattern, one volt per pattern, added to the pattern knob
Changes how many of the auto-player's notes are played, ±5V added to the density knob
A rise strikes that string on its own
Picks the scale, one volt per scale, with 0V leaving the tunings free

outputs.text: The left side of the eight strings mixed, soft-clipped so that eight bowed strings cannot spike past what follows
The right side of the eight strings mixed, soft-clipped so that eight bowed strings cannot spike past what follows
That string on its own jack

notes: the display is the instrument: strumming with the mouse, and setting each string's tuning, decay, stiffness, pick position, exciter and level, all happen there rather than on a control
the exciter is a continuous axis through hammer, pluck, bow and wind rather than a switch, and it is set per string on the display's EXCITE tab
the mouse's height on the PLAY tab is where along the string it is struck: near the bridge at the top, thin and nasal, and over the neck at the bottom, round and hollow
menu: Tuning — a submenu of preset tunings for the eight strings
Mouse strum: Hover over the strings, Click and drag only — chooses whether moving the pointer across the strings plays them or a button has to be held
Hover plays when Rack is in the background — lets the pointer play the strings while another application is in front; off by default, since hover events keep arriving
Stereo width — sets how far the eight strings are spread across the stereo image
Auto rate (no clock patched) — sets the auto-player's free-running speed for when nothing is in the clock jack
